oneliner.t: Public-health physician-trained epidemiologist, former Detroit health director and former Wayne County health, human and veterans services director who narrowly won the Aug. 4, 2026 Democratic primary for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat and faces Republican Mike Rogers on Nov. 3.

hometown.t: Detroit area / Southeast Michigan (graduated Andover High School, Bloomfield Hills, 2003)

upbringing.t: Born in Rochester Hills to Mohamed El-Sayed, an engineer who came from Alexandria, Egypt, for graduate study at Wayne State, and Fatten El-Komy; he was raised in the Detroit area by his father and his stepmother, Jacqueline Johnson, an engineer from Gratiot County. He graduated from Andover High School in Bloomfield Hills in 2003, where he was a three-sport athlete and captain. He then earned a University of Michigan bachelor's degree (biology and political science, 2007), a Rhodes Scholarship to Oxford (DPhil, 2011) and a Columbia M.D. (2014). He did not do a residency and is not licensed to practice medicine.

platform.t: Medicare for All: automatic, universal coverage with no premiums, copays or deductibles, covering vision, dental and hearing; does not ban union or employer supplemental plans. Repeal the Medicaid and ACA subsidy cuts in the 2025 budget law, expand drug-price negotiation to all drugs and patients, end PBMs, and break up healthcare monopolies.
Overturn Citizens United, ban outside spending by super PACs, 527s and corporate 501(c)(4)s, and create public financing and spending caps. Says his campaign takes no corporate money.

Tax capital gains and inheritances over $1 million as ordinary income, add a billionaire wealth tax, lift the Social Security payroll cap, and create a cost-of-living tax exemption of up to $50,000. Wants stronger antitrust enforcement and targeted, sunsetting tariffs, and criticizes Trump's tariffs.

Federal AI rules including frontier-model safety testing, incident reporting and an FDA-style AI agency. Opposes approving more data centers without federal guardrails and wants binding 'terms of engagement' to keep utility rates down.
A national building boom, easier zoning, a federal renter bill of rights, and bans on large corporate ownership of homes and on algorithmic rent-setting software.
Opposes vouchers. Supports universal childcare and pre-K, fully funded IDEA, and a $60,000 minimum teacher salary.

Abolish the filibuster, impose Supreme Court term limits and equal appointments per presidential term, use federal nonpartisan redistricting, oppose the SAVE Act voter-ID bill, and automatically register voters at 18.
Abolish ICE, which he calls a 'paramilitary force', while backing 'certain kinds' of border enforcement.
Opposes 'blank-check' funding of foreign militaries, naming Israel, Egypt, Jordan and Saudi Arabia, and says U.S. weapons are used in a genocide in Gaza.
Codify Roe-era abortion rights in federal law; protect reproductive and gender-affirming care.
Cap farm subsidies at $250,000 per individual and reinvest in family and specialty farms; supports the Farm Workforce Modernization Act and federal right-to-repair.

promises.t: Repeal the Medicaid and ACA subsidy cuts in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' Act.
Pass legislation to overturn Citizens United and ban super PAC outside spending.
Enact a billionaire wealth tax and tax capital gains over $1 million as ordinary income.
Raise the minimum teacher salary to at least $60,000.
Pass his data-center 'Terms of Engagement' proposal as federal law.

record.t: Born in Rochester Hills in 1984 and raised in the Detroit area.

claims.claim: Raised by his father, Mohamed, an Egyptian immigrant, and his stepmother, Jackie.

record.t: Father Mohamed El-Sayed came from Alexandria, Egypt; he was raised by his father and stepmother Jacqueline Johnson.

claims.claim: His stepmother's family has lived in Gratiot County since the 1800s.

record.t: Records confirm she is a Gratiot County native; the family's 1800s roots were not independently found.

claims.claim: Graduated from the University of Michigan with highest distinction.

record.t: U-M bachelor's (2007), Phi Beta Kappa with highest distinction; he gave the commencement address.

claims.claim: Played on the Wolverines men's lacrosse team.

record.t: No independent roster record was found in this pass.

claims.claim: Earned his medical degree from Columbia on an NIH-funded fellowship.

record.t: Columbia M.D. in 2014, supported by the Medical Scientist Training Program (an NIH program) and a Soros fellowship. He did no residency and is not licensed to practice.

claims.claim: Earned a second doctorate at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar.

record.t: Rhodes Scholarship announced in Nov. 2008; Oxford DPhil in 2011.

claims.claim: Rebuilt the Detroit Health Department after the city's bankruptcy.

record.t: Records confirm Mayor Duggan appointed him health officer in Aug. 2015; he served about two years (Bridge also says 18 months). 'Rebuilt' is a characterization.

claims.claim: Restructured Wayne County's Department of Health, Human & Veterans Services, which serves 1.8 million people.

record.t: He directed the department from Dec. 2022/Mar. 2023 to Apr. 2025. How much he 'restructured' it was not documented.

claims.claim: Secured free glasses for kids who needed them.

record.t: He worked with the nonprofit Vision to Learn, which says it gave more than 5,000 glasses to Detroit students.

claims.claim: Removed lead from Detroit's elementary schools.

record.t: He pushed school and child-care water lead testing and expanded child lead testing. His department reported fewer young children with elevated lead levels in 2016. Bridge does not document lead 'removal' from schools.

claims.claim: Made Narcan universally accessible.

record.t: Wayne County's Well Wayne Stations program (2024) lists 96 stations at 92 locations and more than 36,000 kits handed out. That is wide access, short of 'universal'.

claims.claim: Spearheaded a program that will cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 Michiganders over two years.

said.where: campaign site Meet Abdul page and site bio

record.t: Bridge's fact check: the Wayne County–Undue Medical Debt partnership has cleared a little over $95 million for more than 100,000 residents since 2024, well short of $700 million.

record.t: No independent record was found in this pass.

record.t: No independent record was found in this pass.

claims.claim: The campaign is '100% funded by people like you — not corporations and would-be oligarchs.'

record.t: FEC records show no corporate or trade-association PAC contributions. Through July 15, 2026, $14.41M of $14.51M came from individuals and $71,845 from other committees, mostly labor, leadership and progressive PACs. After the primary, the DSCC gave $62,000 directly and spent $328,537 in coordinated expenditures (Aug. 2026). So 'not corporations' holds, but '100% people' is not literal.

entries.t: On his podcast (Jan. 2024), called the Gaza war a 'public health catastrophe' and called for a ceasefire.
In April 2026 on CNN, called both Israeli and Hamas leadership 'evil'. By July 2026 he called Israel a 'rogue state', said the U.S. should stop funding its military, and described Gaza as a genocide.
At the Oct. 8 debate, asked whether he would send weapons if Israel were attacked, said he does not want tax dollars funding war abroad.
During the primary he said he never supported 'defund the police' and was criticized for having promoted the movement earlier (dates of the earlier posts not established in this pass).
Co-authored 'Medicare for All: A Citizen's Guide' advocating single-payer.
Says his Medicare for All plan would let workers keep supplemental private plans through unions or employers.
Posted on X that Rogers 'took a $14 million payout as a pharma lobbyist'. PolitiFact rated it Pants on Fire.
After Rogers' June 22 cease-and-desist letter, partly retracted in a video, saying Rogers is not a pharma lobbyist.

aipac_endorse.t: Not endorsed. AIPAC backed his primary rival Haley Stevens, and AIPAC's super PAC spent against him. His campaign says he has never met with AIPAC or sought its support (as of 2026-10-14).

statements.t: Called Gaza a 'public health catastrophe' and urged a ceasefire.
Called Israel a 'rogue state' and said the U.S. should stop funding foreign militaries, including Israel's.
Said his commitment to Jewish safety equals his commitment to his daughters' safety. The Michigan Jewish Democratic Caucus said his AIPAC criticism worked as a 'dog whistle'.
In the debate, called 'which is more dangerous, Iran or Israel' a 'ridiculous question'.

note.t: 2026 candidate report (filed July 27, 2026, inside a 90-day extension to Aug. 15): earned income of about $407,000, including Wayne County salary ($82,749) plus $72,000 in consulting after he resigned, One Health Management consulting ($82,000), and AME Higher LLC salary and draws ($167,000). Valued assets total $882K–$2.23M: an Ann Arbor rental condo held in a family trust ($250K–$500K), retirement and 529 accounts, his LLCs, and spouse-owned rental homes in Bangalore, India, and Dubai, UAE ($100K–$250K each). Liabilities are a 2008 mortgage ($50K–$100K) and a spouse developer balance in Dubai ($50K–$100K). Net worth = valued assets minus liabilities from the disclosure ranges. He says the foreign properties are his wife's family's, inherited.

checks.legal: Courts: CourtListener direct search was blocked for this tool (provenance), and Justia and Michigan court searches were not run. News: the only court matter found is his own 2018 Wayne County Circuit Court request for a declaratory judgment on his governor eligibility (NY voter registration 2012–2015). The Bureau of Elections rejected Shri Thanedar's challenge in May 2018 and found his Michigan registration continuous, and the state asked the Court of Appeals to drop his request. That is not a charge or liability, so it is not listed under legal. No case naming him as defendant was found in news. Ethics: as a former Detroit and Wayne County appointee, local ethics boards were not searched. The attacks on his mother at the Oct. 8 debate concern a relative. Per TheGrio and Snopes, she was never charged, and her record is not his.
checks.foreign: FARA bulk files (registrants, short forms, foreign principals) searched for an exact-name match on 2026-10-13: none. Senate eFD 2025 and 2026 candidate reports opened (via Free Beacon-hosted copies): spouse-owned rental homes in Bangalore and Dubai, a spouse Mumbai bank account, and a spouse developer balance with a Dubai firm. No foreign income or foreign positions for the candidate.
checks.claims: Mechanical v2.1 sample: (a) every checkable claim on abdulforsenate.com/about (20 listed; 19 rated); (b) the Priorities page (abdulforsenate.com/priorities) has only one checkable claim among its first 10 statements ('100% funded by people'), so its first linked sub-page, Money Out of Politics, was read too (one checkable claim: 'only candidate never taken corporate money'); (c) ad spend per ad is unknown, so the two most-covered ads were used: the June 2026 first TV ad and the Aug. 2026 first general-election ad. Neither ad was quoted, so only the content described in coverage was rated.
checks.democracy: Never served in Congress, so no certification votes. No public statements on 2020/2024 results were searched specifically, and none surfaced in the coverage read.

foreign.t: His own Senate disclosures list spouse-owned rental homes in Bangalore, India, and Dubai, UAE ($100K–$250K each, $5K–$15K rental income each), a spouse savings account in Mumbai, and a 2025 spouse balance with Dubai developer Majid Al Futtaim ($50K–$100K). He says these are his wife's family's inherited properties. The assets are hers; no joint ownership is listed for these items.

research_notes: NOMINATION CONFIRMED: won the Aug. 4, 2026 Democratic primary 744,952 (48.45%) to Haley Stevens' 731,160 (47.55%). McMorrow had withdrawn (4.0%). AP called it Aug. 5 and Stevens conceded and endorsed him. MONEY: FEC totals run through the July 15 pre-primary report (Q3 report due Oct. 15, not yet in the supplied data). The itemized/unitemized individual split, industries, employers and quarters were not available (fec.gov and OpenSecrets blocked). 'other' = receipts − individuals − committees. Committee money: no corporate or trade PACs. Labor, leadership and progressive PACs total about $88K by filing date through July 15, and more after. MONEY FLAGS: set to {} because no corporate/trade PAC money and no country-organized PAC money were found in FEC committee data. One small item needs a human check: a $1,500 contribution (June 3, 2026) from the 'American Committee for Middle East Rights' PAC. The country-word test did not flag it, and its organizing purpose was not verified. Citizens Against AIPAC Corruption spent $57,722 supporting him (an anti-lobby group, not a country lobby). The funders of the super PACs supporting him (WinSenate, AB PAC, Lower Costs Now, etc.) were not retrieved. OUTSIDE: Newsweek (Oct. 7) puts total disclosed race spending above $205M. OUTSIDE THE CLAIMS SAMPLE (recorded for balance, not rated): PolitiFact rated Pants on Fire his June 14, 2026 X post that Rogers took a '$14 million payout as a pharma lobbyist'. He partly walked it back after a cease-and-desist letter. Politico and Bridge reported that he calls himself a 'physician' without a medical license. In the Oct. 8 debate, Rogers' claims tying him to the Muslim Brotherhood were reported as debunked by fact-checkers (TheGrio), and Bridge found no evidence of a connection. His father-in-law gave $200,000 to the pro-El-Sayed Fighting for Michigan PAC (per Wikipedia citing the Free Beacon/Detroit News). That is a relative's donation, not his own. DEBATES: first general-election debate Oct. 8 (WOOD-TV, Grand Rapids); a second is planned but undated. He also did five primary debates/forums. NOT FOUND/NOT DONE: CourtListener/Justia (blocked or not run), local ethics boards, FEC RFAI status, statements on 2020/2024 election results, town-hall counts, campaign photo.
